title: Heterogeneous power profiles + stage-aware prefill/decode scheduler for attention fusion
creator: Marco Alvarez
description:
Problem statement: Our end-to-end latency and token cost vary significantly across GPU SKUs and MIG partition layouts when serving decoder-only models with long prefill phases and short decode steps. The current kernel-selection heuristic prefers a single kernel variant per model/width and does not account for stage-specific characteristics (prefill vs decode) or per-GPU power/clock limits. That causes suboptimal kernel choices on L40S and A10 at default clocks and on H100 when MIG partitions are used.

Goal: Implement a stage-aware scheduler and per-device power profile mechanism that selects kernel variants and clock targets differently for prefill and decode, and tunes MIG partition allocations and clock Governors to maximize tokens/sec under our latency SLOs. The change should be transparent to callers (no API changes) and reversible via rollout flags.

Scope: Implement runtime heuristics that consider: device SKU, MIG partition size, current clock caps, model sequence-length distribution, and stage (prefill vs decode). Add an experiment harness to sweep clock ceilings and kernel combos. Provide console metrics and a rollout plan for canarying behavior.

Out-of-scope: Model-level architecture changes, training adjustments, or external scheduler changes outside the serving runtime.

Notes: This work ties to the kernel-selection and KV-cache routing subsystems and should interoperate with automatic batching and prefix K/V caching layers.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end p50 token latency during decode does not regress by more than 3% on any SKU compared to current baseline when feature is disabled via toggle.
Throughput (tokens/sec) improves by >=12% on average for long-prefill workloads on H100 MIG partitions and >=8% on L40S/A10 for our benchmark set.
No increase in tail latency (p99) >10% across synthetic and in-situ request traces used in production canaries.
Feature gated with runtime flag; default rollout is off. Console shows per-route kernel choice histogram and per-device power profile applied.
Automated A/B canary tools detect regressions and auto-rollback if p99 latency exceeds threshold for 5 minutes.
Documentation updated: runtime kernel-selection doc, ops runbook for MIG + clock tuning, and experiment notebooks linked.
Cross-check with security and audit: changes do not expose secrets; configuration writes to existing config stores and respects RBAC.

progress_updates: 2024-11-22: Triage meeting — agreed on KPI matrix (p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, cost-per-token) and experiment hardware list (2x H100, 3x L40S, 2x A10).
2024-11-28: Design doc posted to Confluence (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runtime/ENG-21548) with kernel candidates (fused_attn_v1/v2, tiled_attn_32, splitKV_prefill).

2024-12-03: Initial prototype switches kernel on stage boundary and collects kernel-selection reason tags in trace spans. Basic telemetry surfaced to tmp-dashboard. Early results: +18% tokens/sec on H100 full-GPU for long-prefill but -4% decode p50 on L40S under default clocks.

2024-12-10: Driver-level instability observed on 80GB H100 MIG 2g. Raised ENG-21690 to investigate NVIDIA driver interaction with aggressive clock management. Workaround: avoid clock ceilings below 80% until driver fix is available.
2024-12-15: Kernel variant catalog expanded to include a low-memory/fewer-warp variant for A10; experiment matrix updated. Preparing sweep scripts for rack-level runs.
2024-12-18: Submitted PR #4672 that adds the stage-aware kernel chooser and telemetry tags; requesting review from @darren and @hannah.
comments: Marco Alvarez (2024-11-22): Added perf objectives and sample workloads. Need to ensure KV cache consistency when switching kernel variants mid-request.
Priya Nair (2024-11-28): Prototype implemented basic stage boundary marker. We need a deterministic fallback if the preferred kernel fails to launch on a given MIG partition.
Darren Lee (2024-12-03): Benchmarked fused_attn_v2 on H100 vs tiled_attn_32 on L40S. Suggest adding clock ceiling sweep to determine knee points rather than single-value tuning.
Hannah Kim (2024-12-10): Observed a CUDA driver kernel launch timeout when clock ceilings set aggressively on MIG 2g. Filed ENG-21690 and patched test harness to skip known-broken configs.
Ops-Bot (2024-12-12): Linked staging console panel — route: /console/runtime/canaries/ENG-21548 (internal only).
Marco Alvarez (2024-12-15): Added acceptance criteria for rollback triggers. We should coordinate with SRE to define incident runbook entries for noisy neighbor scenarios on MIG.
Priya Nair (2024-12-18): PR #4672 is ready; reviewers requested. Next: schedule rack-level sweeps on 2024-12-22 to capture networking jitter effects on long-prefill workloads.
notes: Implementation details: the scheduler will expose two dimensions for kernel selection: (1) stage (prefill|decode), (2) device-class fingerprint {sku, mig_size, clock_ceiling}. The kernel chooser returns a variant id and a recommended clock ceiling — the runtime applies the clock via existing hw-manager API with safety checks.
Telemetry: add 'kernel.variant' and 'kernel.reason' tags to tracing spans, and a per-device 'power_profile_applied' metric. Console should allow searching by kernel.variant to correlate regressions.
Rollback: a runtime toggle disables stage-aware selection and reverts to legacy single-variant selection. Canary gating will be handled via rollout service.
